money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency of the Czech Republic is the Koruna (CZK). Payments by card are common and accepted in most places. Change money at official marked exchange offices such as banks and exchange bureaus. Declare any foreign currency valued at 10,000 euros or more if you're travelling between the Czech Republic and any non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't declare, or if you give wrong information, authorities will fine you. You should check with local authorities in the countries you are leaving, entering or passing through whether you must declare higher amo

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Czechia is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

The UCL (civil aviation authority) registers operators at dron.caa.gov.cz. An operator cannot be registered in more than one EU state, and the registration is valid across Europe. UCL pages say operators based in a third country are registered in its system; an older FAQ says a non-EU resident registers in the first EU country where they will fly, so confirm with the UCL.
Two maps cover zones: DroneView (dronview.rlp.cz, run by the air navigation provider, for pre-flight checks) and the UCL's own digital map of geographical zones.
